title: How VAC authorization for TMS works in British Columbia
summary: An outline of how Veterans, clinicians and the clinic typically move from a first conversation to documentation, preauthorization and a written decision. Clinical and coverage details remain pending medical review.
keyPoints: This draft is an editorial brief, not a finished clinical article.
Clinical suitability, funding eligibility, preauthorization and treatment availability are different questions.
Authorization and payment are not guaranteed.

children.text: Medical content, references and final wording are pending review. Do not publish this article until that work is complete.

body.caption: A typical pathway: conversation, psychiatric assessment, documentation and preauthorization, then a written decision and treatment scheduling.

body.heading: A typical authorization pathway
body.intro: This sequence is a planning outline. Individual cases vary, and a listed step does not mean funding is assured.

steps.title: Initial conversation
steps.body: A first discussion of symptoms, previous treatment and whether a specialist assessment may be appropriate.

steps.title: Psychiatric assessment
steps.body: A psychiatrist-led assessment considers diagnosis, treatment history and whether TMS may be clinically suitable.

steps.title: Documentation and preauthorization
steps.body: Supporting documentation is prepared for the relevant funding pathway. Preauthorization is a separate decision from clinical suitability.

steps.title: Written decision and treatment scheduling
steps.body: If authorization is granted, treatment can be scheduled. If it is not, the clinical options can still be reviewed.

body.heading: Coverage and authorization
body.suitability: Whether TMS is an appropriate treatment depends on diagnosis, previous care and individual medical factors.
body.funding: Funding eligibility is determined by the relevant program. Clinic support with paperwork is not the same as eligibility.
body.preauthorization: Preauthorization is a decision made by the funder after documentation is reviewed. It is not automatic.
body.availability: Treatment can be offered only when it is clinically appropriate and the clinic can provide it. Authorization does not by itself create a treatment slot.

children.text: This brief does not describe a guaranteed outcome, a guaranteed approval, or a completed medical review of VAC policy.

title: TMS for depression when PTSD and anxiety are also present
summary: A planned discussion of how depression, trauma-related symptoms and anxiety can overlap, and why TMS evidence is not the same for every condition. Medical content and references are not yet complete.
keyPoints: Symptoms often overlap; assessment should hold the full picture.
Established evidence for TMS is not equal across every diagnosis.
This draft must not be published until medical content and references are complete.

children.text: When medication and psychotherapy have not provided enough improvement, TMS may offer another evidence-based treatment approach without medication-related sedation. How far that statement extends in the presence of PTSD or anxiety remains to be written against reviewed evidence.

body.caption: Depression, trauma-related symptoms, anxiety, sleep disturbance and functional impairment can overlap. The diagram does not imply equal TMS evidence for each condition.

children.text: Do not imply that TMS has equal evidence for depression, PTSD and anxiety. Comparative statements require reviewed references.
